title: Close the selected BIT caller numerical phase envelope
body:
PR2821 leaves the first-range caller's child-entry, non-ADD and successful-return numerical lifetimes open. This source-bound proof closes those phases: child callbacks retain exactly **18 good / 19 fallback index Words** above every `Consumer.apply` entry resident, including the fallback's zero half-width Word.

Conditional on the unchanged credited component contracts, complete successful calls satisfy

```text
occupied non-LEFT numerical content
<= (L_R+1)r + (L_I+1)i + max(37672r+34i, 20494r+41i).
```

The two templates are charged once; r/i include RIGHT. The coordinatewise allowance is `(37672 residues,41 indices)`. Setup briefly reaches nine indices before retaining eight. The composed envelope is an upper bound, with no simultaneous/global sharpness claim.

Validation at `b553e912bcddef550d9fae6033041ff683399ebe`:

- Registered CPython 3.12 replay: 386,856 caller trace events, 60 sampled callback entries, ten complete small Boolean primitive fixtures and 12 defect-control groups.
- Separate AI integer trace checker: 178,124 events, including all good ranks 1..42 and every ordered fallback endpoint pair; allocation/interior/return controls pass.
- All three commands pass in a read-only Git-free CPython 3.14 export with empty PATH. Source/proof bytes, typed receipts and effective stale-bytecode controls pass; selected-record bindings and post-commit metadata pass.

The actual caller probe abstracts coefficient bodies and payload/record movement; the small primitive fixtures execute their complete payloads. Fixture metadata does not prove selected catalogue membership. The all-domain conclusion is the written conditional source proof, not a full GL64 execution, human/formal-kernel proof, physical reserve, supplier admission or new kappa. Next: join the nonnumerical/physical categories at the same chronological cuts and bind the larger recursive/outer consumer.

Credit Jose Manuel/jmbarrancoml PR2697; Nick Petalas PR2759/2770/2778/2781/2801/2815; Arham Tahir PR2796; Ross Richardson PR2810/2821; David Arias and all retained source notices. New work by Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance and a separate storage-lifetimes AI specialist, Apache-2.0. One new opt-in package; no predecessor or selected-frontier changes.

[Canonical investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2319#discussioncomment-18961346). Scientific base `cfddb858` is deliberately retained; submission main `fbdbcb53` at 2026-10-16 00:09 UTC had unchanged relevant guidance/selected/runner bytes and no package collision. Metadata overlap completely paginated 690 open PRs, 1467 Discussion records and 2105 local records at 00:09–00:12 UTC, no warnings; arbitrary diffs/unpublished work remain outside coverage. All six predecessor heads were rechecked unchanged. Hosted CI is a separate pending gate.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-child-caller-lifetime`.

Task `independent-moment`, scope **changed**: the live PR2821 handoff replaces a redundant rank-root calculation with the missing caller-resident accounting implication. Exact runtime `a53fdf4bcbe33c6732f0bec1badc8c023380f9d1`; [TASK and freshness](https://github.com/RossRichardson/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b553e912bcddef550d9fae6033041ff683399ebe/research/selected-child-caller-lifetime/TASK.json), [all exact dependency heads](https://github.com/RossRichardson/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b553e912bcddef550d9fae6033041ff683399ebe/research/selected-child-caller-lifetime/evidence/DEPENDENCIES.json), and [proof plus next questions](https://github.com/RossRichardson/integer-mult-bounds/tree/b553e912bcddef550d9fae6033041ff683399ebe/research/selected-child-caller-lifetime) provide the reviewable source boundary.
